courses.title: Ihsan & Character: A Practical Beginning
courses.subject: Tasawwuf
courses.description: Build a thoughtful routine around intention, worship and everyday character through short lessons and knowledge checks.
courses.certificate: Local study completion record only; not accredited or an ijazah.
outcomes: Explain Ihsan and the purpose of purification.
Recognize common harmful habits without judging other people’s hearts.
Apply practical manners to family, work and community life.
Read introductory texts with context and appropriate guidance.
Maintain a manageable routine without treating progress as spiritual rank.
courses.prerequisites: No formal prerequisites. Continue learning practical worship with reliable scholarship.

lessons.title: Ihsan and the purpose of learning
lessons.body:
Tasawwuf is approached here as learning about purification, sincere worship and good character. The Hadith of Jibril describes Ihsan through awareness of Allah. Begin with faith, worship and responsibilities; unusual experiences are not a learning goal. Terms and teaching methods differ between scholars and communities.

Practice
Notice one ordinary responsibility you can carry out with more care today.

Reflection
How would better character change my reason for studying?

quiz.question: What is the main focus of this introductory path?
quiz.explanation: Sincere worship and good character. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Obligations before extra practices
lessons.body:
A learning plan should support the duties you already owe. Optional routines should not cause missed prayers, neglected family responsibilities or dishonesty at work. Ask a qualified scholar about the worship rules that apply to you instead of replacing fiqh with a spiritual exercise.

Practice
List your essential responsibilities and choose a realistic time for study.

Reflection
Is an optional routine crowding out something I owe another person?

quiz.question: What should optional practices support?
quiz.explanation: Obligatory duties and responsible conduct. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Renewing intention
lessons.body:
A good outward action can be weakened by a desire for attention. Intention is renewed before and during work, learning and worship. Do the helpful action without turning the examination of motives into endless hesitation; noticing a mixed motive is a reason to gently redirect it.

Practice
Choose one useful action and privately renew why you are doing it.

Reflection
Would I still do this if nobody praised me?

quiz.question: What is a helpful response to noticing a mixed motive?
options: Renew the intention and continue the good
quiz.explanation: Renew the intention and continue the good. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Repentance with hope
lessons.body:
Repentance joins hope with responsibility. Recognize the wrong, stop it, regret it and resolve not to return. When another person's rights are involved, seek sound guidance on restitution and repair. Repeated mistakes call for renewed effort, rather than despair or a public performance of guilt.

Practice
Identify one practical step that prevents a repeated mistake; avoid recording private sins.

Reflection
What can I repair rather than merely regret?

resources.title: Quran 59:18: consider what you send ahead

quiz.question: Which response best reflects repentance?
options: Stop the wrong and work to repair harm
quiz.explanation: Stop the wrong and work to repair harm. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Presence in prayer
lessons.body:
Prayer and character belong together. Prepare calmly where possible, learn the meaning of a short portion you recite and return attention when it wanders. Distraction does not make a person worthless. Learn the legal requirements of prayer from a reliable teacher while gradually strengthening attention.

Practice
Learn the meaning of one phrase you use in prayer.

Reflection
What preparation helps me arrive at prayer less hurried?

quiz.question: What should you do when attention wanders?
quiz.explanation: Gently return attention. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Remembrance and Quran reflection
lessons.body:
Remembrance can accompany daily life without becoming a competition. Read a manageable portion of Quran with meaning, and use established supplications you understand. The study timings in this course are planning suggestions, not newly prescribed ritual numbers or promises of special rewards.

Practice
Read a short passage with its meaning and note one action it encourages.

Reflection
How can remembrance affect my next conversation?

quiz.question: How should this course's study timings be understood?
quiz.explanation: Flexible planning suggestions. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Guarding the tongue
lessons.body:
Before speaking or posting, consider truth, benefit and harm. Silence can be better than insult or gossip, but it must not become an excuse to ignore injustice. Advice should be accurate, proportionate and offered with care; a private disagreement need not become public humiliation.

Practice
Pause before forwarding one message and check whether it is true and useful.

Reflection
Did my words help, or did I merely want the last word?

quiz.question: Which habit best protects speech?
options: Checking truth, benefit and possible harm
quiz.explanation: Checking truth, benefit and possible harm. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Listening and disagreement
lessons.body:
Good manners include listening long enough to understand a view before answering. Disagreement in scholarship should be described accurately. You can ask for evidence and preserve boundaries without contempt, personal attacks or claiming to know another person's intention.

Practice
Summarize another person's point fairly before replying.

Reflection
Can I disagree without making the other person feel small?

quiz.question: What is a constructive way to disagree?
options: Understand the view and respond respectfully
quiz.explanation: Understand the view and respond respectfully. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Humility without self-contempt
lessons.body:
Humility means accepting truth and treating people with dignity. It does not require denying your abilities, accepting abuse or abandoning responsibility. Notice the wish to be above others, then choose a task or conversation in which service matters more than status.

Practice
Accept one useful correction without immediately defending yourself.

Reflection
Where do I confuse being respected with being superior?

quiz.question: Which action shows humility?
quiz.explanation: Accepting a truthful correction. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Envy and wishing others well
lessons.body:
Envy becomes harmful when another person's blessing feels like a loss you want removed. Notice the comparison and redirect it toward gratitude and permissible effort. Admiring a good example and working toward similar good need not involve wishing harm to the other person.

Practice
Make a sincere dua for someone whose success triggers comparison.

Reflection
What good can I pursue without wishing anyone a loss?

quiz.question: Which response helps counter destructive envy?
options: Wish others well and pursue good lawfully
quiz.explanation: Wish others well and pursue good lawfully. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Anger and self-command
lessons.body:
Strength includes restraint when anger rises. A pause can prevent speech or actions that require repair later. Address the issue when you can speak clearly. Restraint does not mean tolerating danger or never seeking help; it means choosing a just response rather than an uncontrolled one.

Practice
Plan one respectful sentence you can use to pause a heated discussion.

Reflection
Which early sign tells me that I need to slow down?

quiz.question: What does the cited hadith associate with real strength?
quiz.explanation: Controlling oneself in anger. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Sincerity and hidden good
lessons.body:
Praise is not a reliable measure of sincerity, and lack of recognition does not erase a useful deed. Keep some ordinary good private when appropriate, while remembering that public service can also be sincere. Avoid judging others merely because their work is visible.

Practice
Do one helpful action without seeking credit for it.

Reflection
Am I using service to help someone or to build an image?

quiz.question: Which statement about public good deeds is sound?
options: They remove the need for accountability
They can be sincere; visibility alone does not reveal intention
quiz.explanation: They can be sincere; visibility alone does not reveal intention. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Patience as steady action
lessons.body:
Patience includes perseverance in good, restraint from wrong and endurance through hardship. It is not passive acceptance of preventable harm. Take appropriate practical steps, seek support when needed and avoid declaring that a difficult feeling is proof of weak faith.

Practice
Choose one difficult but useful task and complete a manageable part.

Reflection
What patient action is possible for me today?

quiz.question: What does patience include?
options: Steady good action alongside appropriate help
quiz.explanation: Steady good action alongside appropriate help. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Gratitude in use, not only words
lessons.body:
Gratitude can be expressed in praise and in the way a blessing is used. Time, ability and relationships offer opportunities for service. Gratitude does not require denying grief, poverty or a problem that needs attention; it can coexist with honest requests for help.

Practice
Use one ability or resource to benefit someone within your means.

Reflection
Which blessing am I treating as an entitlement?

quiz.question: Which is a practical expression of gratitude?
options: Using a blessing responsibly for good
quiz.explanation: Using a blessing responsibly for good. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Trust with responsible effort
lessons.body:
Reliance on Allah belongs with consultation, decisions and action. Make a reasonable plan, use lawful means and accept that outcomes are not fully controlled by you. Trust is not an instruction to neglect preparation, medical care or obligations.

Practice
Take one reasonable step on a concern, then make dua without demanding a particular outcome.

Reflection
What is my responsibility, and what is outside my control?

quiz.question: What belongs with reliance on Allah?
options: A guarantee of the desired result
quiz.explanation: Responsible effort and consultation. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Hope, fear and returning
lessons.body:
A healthy learning path makes room for hope and accountability. Remembering mercy should support repentance, not excuse harm. Awareness of consequences should encourage repair, not despair. If an exercise fuels persistent distress, simplify it and speak to an appropriate trusted professional or teacher.

Practice
Replace one hopeless self-judgment with a specific next step toward repair.

Reflection
What would hopeful responsibility look like this week?

resources.title: Quran 59:18: consider what you send ahead

quiz.question: Which balance does this lesson encourage?
quiz.explanation: Hope with accountability. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Kindness in family life
lessons.body:
Character is tested in familiar relationships as well as formal gatherings. Speak respectfully, share responsibilities and recognize the needs of people around you. Respect does not remove personal safety or lawful boundaries. Discuss difficult family duties with someone qualified who understands the situation.

Practice
Carry out one agreed household responsibility without seeking praise.

Reflection
Who experiences the everyday version of my character?

quiz.question: Where should good character be practiced?
options: In family life as well as public settings
quiz.explanation: In family life as well as public settings. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Service without humiliation
lessons.body:
Helping others should preserve their dignity. Ask what is useful instead of assuming, protect privacy and avoid reminding people of favors. Service includes time and attention as well as money. Give within your means without neglecting responsibilities or making unsupported promises.

Practice
Offer one practical, welcome form of help and respect a refusal.

Reflection
Did I preserve the other person's choice and dignity?

quiz.question: What should accompany service?
quiz.explanation: Respect for dignity and privacy. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Companionship and teacher selection
lessons.body:
Good companionship encourages honesty, learning and responsible conduct. A teacher should welcome reasonable questions, explain sources and respect boundaries. No claim of spiritual authority removes ordinary accountability. This introductory path does not assign an order, initiation or private devotional regimen.

Practice
Write three questions about a prospective teacher's learning, methods and accountability.

Reflection
Can I ask questions and decline a request without coercion?

quiz.question: What is a healthy sign in a teacher?
options: Respect for questions, evidence and boundaries
quiz.explanation: Respect for questions, evidence and boundaries. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Reading classical works responsibly
lessons.body:
Classical books use technical vocabulary, report earlier experiences and may include narrations needing verification. Read the introduction and a reliable explanation before treating a passage as practical instruction. Metaphor, history and legal rulings are not interchangeable, and a translation is an interpretation of its source.

Practice
Choose a short passage and note one term to ask a teacher about.

Reflection
Am I treating an unfamiliar expression as a rule without context?

quiz.question: How should a difficult classical passage be approached?
options: As proof no teacher is needed
As a reason to dismiss all other scholarship
With context, explanation and source checking
quiz.explanation: With context, explanation and source checking. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Gentle self-accounting
lessons.body:
Self-accounting asks what helped, what harmed and what can be repaired. Keep the review brief and practical. A useful review names an action rather than condemning your entire identity. Private confessions are not required, and this app does not rank the purity of a person's heart.

Practice
Review one helpful action, one repair and one next step without writing sensitive details.

Reflection
What small change would make tomorrow more honest or kind?

resources.title: Quran 59:18: consider what you send ahead

quiz.question: What is useful self-accounting?
options: A brief review leading to repair
quiz.explanation: A brief review leading to repair. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Awareness in ordinary work
lessons.body:
Awareness of Allah can inform study, employment, trade and care work. Look for honesty in promises, time and responsibilities. This course uses muraqabah in the introductory sense of watchfulness over conduct; specialized contemplative methods belong with qualified guidance, not automatic app instructions.

Practice
Choose one work or study commitment and fulfill it accurately.

Reflection
Where could greater honesty change the way I use my time?

resources.title: Quran 59:18: consider what you send ahead

quiz.question: How is watchfulness introduced here?
options: A claim to know unseen matters
quiz.explanation: Awareness that improves ordinary conduct. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: A sustainable personal routine
lessons.body:
A modest routine can be easier to maintain than a dramatic beginning. Choose a realistic amount of reading and reflection that fits your responsibilities. Missed days do not erase learning. Resume gently and revise the plan when circumstances change instead of escalating it to protect a streak.

Practice
Write a flexible one-week plan with room for rest and essential duties.

Reflection
Can I continue this routine during an ordinary busy week?

quiz.question: What makes a routine sustainable?
options: Treating a missed day as total failure
quiz.explanation: Realistic effort with flexibility. Review the lesson and its source references.

lessons.title: Continuing with humility
lessons.body:
Completion marks study activity, not sainthood, salvation or superiority. Revisit the foundations, keep learning practical fiqh and seek qualified explanation for advanced texts. Choose one area of conduct to improve over the next month and assess it by responsibility and service rather than unusual experiences.

Practice
Select one topic to revisit, one book to read and one question for a teacher.

Reflection
What has changed in how I treat people?

quiz.question: What does course completion mean?
quiz.explanation: Completion of study activities only. Review the lesson and its source references.
